data.title: SpaceX Moves to Stop Disclosure of $16.8B Terafab Project Documents in Texas
data.description:
SpaceX has gone to court in Texas to block the release of documents related to its Terafab facility. The company claims general accessibility will reveal sensitive information, putting the project at risk.

Elon Musk’s SpaceX is building a gigantic $16.5 billion chip factory in Grimes County. The company, however, wants to keep some aspects of the project secret. In its application suing the Attorney General and county, SpaceX wants to deter two public records requests seeking ‘sensitive’ information on costs, staffing, land acquisition, and technical details.

In the lawsuit before the Travis County District Court, SpaceX argues it competes in many markets. As such, some of the company’s deals “are competitively sensitive: their disclosure would reveal SpaceX’s costs, plans and negotiating strategy to competitors and to every other jurisdiction with which SpaceX negotiates.”

Local resident Vanessa Burzynski submitted a public records request in May under the Texas Public Information Act. Fellow Grimes County resident Marie Egyed filed their own request in June. Both of them want details of SpaceX’s communications with the county.

SpaceX approached the courts after AG Ken Paxton approved the release of some of the requested documents.

Terafab will produce semiconductors for autonomous vehicles, humanoid robots like Optimus, and extra-terrestrial data centers. Upon completion, the complex will cover 100 million square feet, making it the world’s largest building, according to Musk. It will employ more than 3,000 people.

The Terafab project enjoys county officials’ support and receives tax breaks. However, some residents oppose the development, arguing it would disrupt their rural lifestyle and crash property values.

data.title: U.S. Lawmaker Calls on NHTSA to Act on Sleeping Tesla Drivers
data.description:
A U.S. lawmaker is calling on federal regulators to take a closer look at Tesla’s driver monitoring safeguards following a growing number of videos showing drivers apparently asleep behind the wheel while using Autopilot or Full Self-Driving (FSD).

Representative Raja Krishnamoorthi, a Democrat from Illinois, sent a letter to U.S. Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy this week asking what the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) is doing to address potential misuse of Tesla’s driver-assistance systems.

The letter follows an NBC News investigation that identified 43 videos appearing to show people asleep behind the wheel of moving Teslas, including 17 posted this year.

Krishnamoorthi argues regulators need to determine whether Tesla has sufficient safeguards against foreseeable misuse.

“FSD requires continuous human supervision, yet the message appears to encourage use of the system precisely when the vehicle has detected that the driver may be less capable,” Krishnamoorthi wrote, referring to Tesla’s “Drowsiness detected. Stay focused with FSD” message.

Similar incidents piling up in B.C.

While Krishnamoorthi’s concerns are directed at U.S. regulators, Canada has seen its own string of incidents, particularly in British Columbia.

At least five separate cases involving allegedly sleeping or significantly distracted Tesla drivers have surfaced in B.C. this year.

In March, police ticketed a Model Y driver who allegedly appeared asleep on Highway 1 in Coquitlam. In July, another driver was ticketed after police spotted them reading documents while using FSD in West Kelowna. That same month, video emerged of a Tesla driver apparently asleep while travelling between Golden and Revelstoke.

Two more incidents were revealed earlier this month. A Maple Ridge woman received a $368 ticket after witnesses allegedly recorded her sleeping behind the wheel on Highway 1 in North Vancouver, while another Tesla driver was ticketed after a B.C. Highway Patrol officer allegedly found him asleep during morning rush hour in Langley.

Krishnamoorthi has asked NHTSA to explain whether it considers the growing collection of sleeping-driver videos evidence of a broader safety problem and how effective Tesla’s driver-monitoring safeguards are at preventing misuse.

data.title: Tesla finally brings Model Y Performance to China
data.description:
Tesla has officially launched the refreshed Model Y Performance in China. While China was the first market to receive the refreshed Juniper Model Y, it has had to wait much longer for the Performance variant, becoming one of the last major markets to get Tesla’s quickest version of the electric SUV.

The new Model Y Performance starts at RMB 369,000 (C$76,150/US$55,000). Tesla is estimating deliveries in just two to six weeks, meaning the first customers could be behind the wheel before the end of September.

As expected, the Performance sits at the top of what is becoming a crowded Model Y lineup in China. It is RMB 30,000 more expensive than the six-seat Model Y L, which starts at RMB 339,000. The lineup now consists of five variants, with the entry-level Rear-Wheel Drive starting at RMB 263,500.

The timing of the launch comes two months after the top-of-the-line variant appeared in a filing with China’s Ministry of Industry and Information Technology (MIIT).

With the new variant, Tesla is hoping to boost Model Y sales, which have been declining in China this year. In August a total of 29,260 units were sold in the country, down nearly 26% from a year earlier and marking the SUV’s third consecutive year-over-year monthly decline. Through the first eight months of 2026, Tesla delivered 226,931 Model Ys in China, down 6.1%.

To further boost sales, Tesla introduced some discounts and finance incentives this week on inventory Model Y and Model 3 vehicles delivered before the end of the quarter.

data.title: SpaceX Signs Another Massive AI Compute Deal Worth $13.3 Billion Per Year
data.description:
SpaceX has added another major customer to its rapidly growing AI compute business, signing a new agreement that will generate approximately US$1.11 billion per month starting December 1, 2026.

SpaceX CFO Bret Johnsen revealed the deal Thursday while speaking at the Goldman Sachs Communacopia and Technology Conference. Johnson did not identify the customer.

“Earlier this month, we closed another hosting deal. By the end of this year, with annualizing our December number, we’re on track to hit $100 billion of ARR,” Johnsen said.

The new contract alone works out to roughly US$13.3 billion in annualized revenue, adding to a growing list of enormous compute agreements SpaceX has signed this year.

Anthropic is paying approximately US$1.25 billion per month for access to SpaceX’s Colossus infrastructure, while Google signed a separate agreement worth US$920 million per month beginning in October. Reflection AI joined the customer list in June with a deal worth US$150 million per month for access to NVIDIA GB300 hardware at Colossus 2 near Memphis, Tennessee.

Including the latest unnamed customer, those four agreements represent about US$3.43 billion in monthly contracted AI compute revenue, or more than US$41 billion on an annualized basis at their stated rates.

The deals are quickly turning AI infrastructure into another major business for SpaceX. Johnson said the company’s Starlink and AI businesses only could generate US$100 billion annual revenue by the end of 2026.

Johnsen also provided several updates on SpaceX’s plans to eventually move some of that computing infrastructure beyond Earth. The company is targeting its first orbital compute satellites for next year, while the upcoming Starship Flight 14 is expected to carry the first operational Starlink V3 satellites, marking the start of revenue-generating Starship missions.

data.title: Tesla starts shipping Cybertruck Powershare integration, but only with Powerwall 3 for now
data.description:
Tesla has started shipping the long-awaited software needed to integrate Cybertruck with Powerwall, allowing the two products to work together to provide significantly more backup power during a grid outage.

However, this initial release is only compatible with Powerwall 3. Cybertruck Lead Engineer Wes Morrill confirmed on Wednesday that the firmware is going out to customers after facing lengthy delays.

The integration essentially turns the Cybertruck and Powerwall 3 into a larger home energy system, with Tesla’s vehicle and energy teams working together to manage power through the same Wall Connector normally used to charge the truck.

Tesla highlighted the potential backup capability through its Cybertruck account, adding that support for owners with Powerwall 2 is coming later this year.

Cybertruck’s Powershare system can provide up to 11.5 kW of continuous power to a home. Tesla estimates the truck can provide more than three days of backup based on typical household consumption of around 30 kWh per day.

The rollout has been a long time coming. Tesla initially expected to enable Powershare compatibility with Powerwall much earlier, before telling owners in December 2025 that development had pushed the release to mid-2026.

Tesla’s website and installation documentation have not yet fully caught up with the rollout, with some pages still describing Powerwall compatibility as “coming soon.”

Tesla’s Canadian Powershare page similarly continues to describe Powerwall compatibility as coming through a future over-the-air (OTA) update.

data.title: BYD’s New Battery Charges to 97% in 12 Minutes at -30°C
data.description:
BYD has demonstrated the cold-weather charging performance of its latest battery technology, charging a Denza Z9GT after the vehicle spent 24 hours at -30°C (-22°F).

The test used BYD’s second-generation Blade Batterykelown connected to one of the automaker’s new 1,500 kW Flash chargers. After sitting at -30°C (-22°F) for 24 hours, the Z9GT was plugged in with a 20% state of charge.

Just 12 minutes later, the battery had reached 97%.

Under ideal conditions, the company says its second-generation Blade Battery can charge from 10% to 70% in about five minutes and reach 97% in under 10 minutes. The extreme cold test added only a few minutes despite the battery starting at -30°C.

While the Denza Z9GT itself isn’t confirmed for Canada, BYD is preparing to enter the Canadian market. The Chinese automaker has been laying the groundwork for its arrival since the new quota import system was announced earlier this year. Most recently, the company launched a Canadian website, indicating its headquarters are in Markham, Ontario.

BYD also appears to have bigger plans than simply selling cars. Earlier this year, Canadian job postings revealed the company was hiring for positions to eventually bring this Flash charging technology to Canada.

The company has already installed over 10,000 Flash charging stations in China in just six months, and plans to double that number by the end of the year.

data.title: Ferrari Luce makes its Canadian debut in Quebec – here’s where it’s going next
data.description:
Ferrari’s first electric vehicle (EV) has officially arrived in Canada, just months after the Luce made its controversial global debut with a design unlike anything previously seen from the Italian automaker.

The Ferrari Luce was recently shown to Ferrari Quebec clients, marking the first known appearance of the electric Ferrari in Canada. The display car was finished in matte grey with gloss-black accents and black wheels.

Ferrari has not yet publicly announced official Canadian pricing, but the Luce is expected to cost around $800,000 in Canada.

View this post on Instagram

A post shared by Canadian Car Registry 🇨🇦 (@canadiancarregistry)

With its first Canadian appearance now complete in Quebec, Drive Tesla has been told the Luce will make its next appearance at the Toronto International Film Festival (TIFF), which starts today and runs until September 20.

The Luce represents a dramatic departure from the low-slung sports cars traditionally associated with Ferrari. Instead, the nearly 198-inch-long EV features four doors, seating for up to five passengers and a rounded, almost hatchback-like profile.

Underneath that unconventional body is a considerably more familiar level of Ferrari performance. Four electric motors combine to produce 1,050 horsepower, while the Luce can accelerate from 0-60 mph in approximately 2.4 seconds. Its 122 kWh battery is expected to provide up to 530 km of range, while an 800-volt electrical architecture supports DC fast charging at up to 350kW.

Despite considerable criticism surrounding its styling, early indications suggest Ferrari isn’t having much trouble finding customers. Ferrari reportedly set an initial 2026 target of just under 500 Luce sales globally and reached that figure within approximately two months of the car’s May unveiling. Demand has reportedly been particularly strong in China, where an initial allocation of 88 vehicles quickly sold out.

The Luce has also already made auction history. A special “Tailor Made” example sold for US$40 million at RM Sotheby’s Monterey auction in August, making it the most expensive new car ever sold at auction. Proceeds from the charity sale went to The Ferrari Foundation.

That record-setting car was purchased by billionaire businessman, inventor and philanthropist Dr. Herbert “Herbie” Wertheim.

data.title: 2027 Nissan LEAF is Canada’s cheapest new EV at $34,998, before EVAP
data.description:
Nissan is making the 2027 LEAF significantly more affordable in Canada, adding a new entry-level S trim that gives the electric crossover a starting price of just $34,998.

That makes the LEAF S the lowest-priced new electric vehicle (EV) in Canada, according to Nissan. It also qualifies for the federal Electric Vehicle Affordability Program (EVAP), dropping its effective price to $29,998 with the $5,000 incentive available in 2026. That amount will be reduced to $4,000 in 2027.

While you get a lower price with the new entry-level LEAF, it also comes with a smaller battery. The rest of the LEAF lineup uses a 75 kWh pack, but the S gets a 53 kWh battery powering a 174-horsepower electric motor. Nissan estimates it will deliver up to 341 km of range.

Moving up to the S+ brings the larger 75 kWh battery, 214 horsepower and up to 488 km of estimated range for $45,198.

2027 Nissan LEAF Canadian Pricing

Despite being the cheapest model, Nissan hasn’t stripped the S of many of the LEAF’s more useful features. It comes standard with dual 12.3-inch displays, wireless Apple CarPlay and Android Auto, a heat pump, battery heater, Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) capability and Nissan Safety Shield 360.

Charging is also notably different from many EVs. The LEAF has separate J1772 and NACS ports, allowing Level 1 and Level 2 AC charging through J1772 while the NACS connection provides access to compatible DC fast chargers.

The S+ and higher trims also receive an upgraded 11 kW onboard charger for 2027, which Nissan says can cut Level 2 charging times by roughly 35%.

The new LEAF S will arrive at Canadian Nissan dealerships this fall.

data.title: BYD’s Canadian Test Fleet Grows with Sealion 7 Sighting
data.description:
A BYD Sealion 7 has been spotted in Markham, Ontario, Canada, adding another model to the automaker’s growing Canadian test fleet.

Photos shared on Reddit the Sealion 7 in an underground parking garage in Markham, not far from BYD Canada’s headquaters at 60 Travail Road. It is believed to be the first sighting of the electric crossover in the area.

The Sealion 7 joins at least two other BYD-family vehicles recently seen in Canada. A Sealion 6 was previously photographed near BYD’s Markham operations with its badges covered, while a Fangchengbao Ti7 was spotted at a Montreal-area hotel alongside another Sealion 7.

What makes the sightings particularly interesting is that none of those models match the vehicles BYD has already been cleared to import into Canada.

Transport Canada’s Appendix G pre-clearance registry includes BYD plants in Shenzhen and Xi’an, covering vehicles such as the Dolphin, Seal, Atto 3 and Seagull. Despite those approvals, none of those models have surfaced in the recent Canadian sightings.

Instead, the Sealion 7, Sealion 6 and Ti7 appear to be smaller-volume evaluation vehicles, potentially entering Canada through case-by-case approvals. Their presence suggests BYD is evaluating a broader range of products than its existing pre-clearance entries would suggest, but does not confirm which models could eventually be offered to Canadian buyers.

The timing also comes as Canada enters the second period of its Chinese EV import quota. Based on unused capacity from the first period, as many as roughly 33,397 vehicles could be available for import between September 2026 and February 2027.

BYD’s Canadian website continues to say “Coming Soon,” with no official pricing, launch date or Canadian retail lineup announced.

data.title: Canada’s $27.6 Billion U.S. Counter-Tariffs Take Effect — What It Means for Tesla
data.description:
Canada’s latest round of counter-tariffs against the United States has officially taken effect, adding duties of up to 50% on C$27.6 billion worth of American goods as trade negotiations between the two countries remain stalled.

The new measures came into force at 12:01 a.m. on September 8 and impose tariffs of 15%, 25% and 50% across a wide range of U.S. products, including steel, dairy, appliances, agricultural equipment, pulp and paper, and electronics. The rates are designed to match tariffs recently imposed by Washington on Canadian goods.

The latest package does not, however, replace Canada’s existing counter-tariffs on American-made vehicles. The Department of Finance specifically confirmed, “Other existing counter-tariffs, including against U.S. autos, will also continue to apply.”

For Tesla buyers in Canada, there is no impact as the company is currently importing Shanghai-built Model 3s under Canada’s new Chinese EV quota. Those vehicles are subject to the regular 6.1% most-favoured-nation tariff rather than the new 15%, 25% or 50% counter-tariffs targeting U.S. goods.

Any imports of U.S.-built Teslas, which as of right now is only the Cybertruck built at Giga Texas after the Model S/X were discontinued earlier this summer, would continue to face Canada’s existing automotive counter-tariff regime.

The September 8 measures therefore create no new Tesla-specific tariff, and Tesla has not announced any Canadian price changes related to the latest package taking effect.
